subtitle: Lay out your album covers
promotionalText: New: repeat any album or playlist, and see your newest albums first when you add to a board. And your Apple Music playlists can sit on a discboard as a single tile.

description.text: Remember pulling LP and CD sleeves out of their cases and spreading them across the floor? You'd put one on, sit with it for a while, set it back down, reach for another. No rush. The floor was the playlist — and looking at the covers was half the fun.
Discboard is that feeling, on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch — and in the car.

Pick an album from your library — or drag one straight in from Apple Music — and set it down on a discboard. Nudge it where you want, pinch it to size, turn it to the angle that feels right. Pull out another. Fan them out, overlap them, tuck a small one behind a big one. Then sit back and look at it — a little arrangement of cover art that's all yours.
Tap a cover and its jewel case lifts off the board and turns around: title, artist, every track. Tap a track and it plays through Apple Music. Then just listen.
It's meant to be slow. A small, deliberate set of albums in front of you instead of an endless scroll — something to sit with, not swipe past.

items: Lay your covers out however you like — drag with one finger, pinch to size, twist to rotate. Or size them all at once by album length or your ratings
Tuck small covers behind big ones with a layer slider, or float a favorite above the pile
Every cover is a real CD jewel case — translucent shell, ribbed spine, and a sheen that drifts across the plastic as you move
Tap a cover to flip it open — full track listing with ratings and favorites, one tap to play any track
Put playlists on a board too — each one a single tile
See a board whichever way suits the moment — the spatial layout, a scrolling list, or a grid of covers, ordered by album, artist, release date, or how they're stacked. Each board keeps its own choice
Take your boards to the car — CarPlay lists your discboards, folders and all, and plays any album, with favorites, star ratings, and Up Next right on the Now Playing screen
On your wrist — on Apple Watch, flip through a board's covers with the Digital Crown, tap one to play it on your iPhone, and rate what's playing
Bring your own wallpaper, or use the bundled set
Share a board — as a file that opens in Discboard as the other person's own copy, as a high-resolution image, or as an animation where the covers sweep or spin into place
Widgets for your Home Screen and Mac desktop — a board, what's playing, or Surprise Me, which plays a random album
A player rides along — shuffle, repeat, a full now-playing view, and a mini-player that stays out of the way while you keep arranging
Works with your whole Apple Music library, including iTunes Match uploads — even cloud-only and uploaded artwork rides across your devices
Your boards, arrangements, wallpapers, and ratings sync across your devices through iCloud
No account to create, no sign-up

description.text: Discboard is free to use — room for a couple of boards and a small collection of covers, enough to get the feeling.
Discboard Premium opens it all the way up: unlimited boards and unlimited covers. Keep one board for late nights, one for road trips, one for the records you're rediscovering — as full as you like.

items: Group your boards into folders — and folders inside folders — as your collection grows
Back up your boards to a file and restore them on another device
Monthly or yearly, with a 7-day free trial

description.text: It's not a streaming service. You bring your Apple Music library; Discboard gives it a place to be looked at and listened to.
Discboard Premium is an auto-renewing subscription.

items: Monthly — $2.99 (US) per month
Annual — $19.99 (US) per year
New subscribers get a 7-day free trial.
